decisions.reason: 목격한다면 is a hypothetical; SOL turns it into a factual gerund about this crash.
SOL drops 그토록 흉포하다는, the reputational ‘said to be so fearsome.’
‘that could scream’ is punchier; ‘capable of screaming’ is stiffer with no fidelity gain.
돌진하는 is a charge/rush, not a plunge.
‘Neither…nor would move’ is more natural frozen-panic English for 발이, 손이 움직이지 않는다.
SOL drops 조차 and 주어지지 않았다 (‘not even given a chance’).
떠오른 supports ‘flashed,’ but SOL omits 그 순간.
decisions.replacement: The same thought flashed through everyone’s mind at that very moment.

decisions.reason: ‘With’ is cleaner than ‘Along with’ for 과 함께.
SOL drops 그 and 최후방 (‘that’ / ‘very rear’).
덩어리 is a mass/hunk; BASE’s ‘object’ is bland and SOL’s ‘behemoth’ is unsupported.
decisions.replacement: The massive hunk of steel, weighing dozens of tons, smashed and burst through everything in its path.

decisions.reason: ‘Green blood spurted from the monsters’ is more natural English word order.
SOL improves 뛰어나다/정도가 있는 법 but adds unsupported ‘giant.’
decisions.replacement: No matter how formidable a monster’s physical defenses were, they had their limits. Nothing could stop the airplane now that it had become a monster blender.

decisions.reason: Keep 섬뜩한 as eerie; 아비규환 is hellish pandemonium, not generic carnage.
decisions.replacement: The eerie sounds of flesh being torn apart swallowed the monsters’ screams. It was a hellish scene unlike anything Shao Shen had ever seen or heard.

decisions.reason: ‘Despite the chaos’ tightens 이런 와중에도 without loss.
Recasts Korean-shaped ‘mana carried in that voice’ and renders 강대한 as immense.
Singular S-rank fits the voice, but 아군이 죽을 것 is allies dying, not him killing them.
decisions.replacement: *To think he’d use a method those island bastards employed back in World War II. Had he not considered that his own allies might die too?*

decisions.reason: 것 같은데 is tentative; BASE is calqued and SOL upgrades it to certainty.
decisions.replacement: *He seemed to have been dispatched by the Central Military Commission… But did our country even have an S-rank Hunter like that?*

decisions.reason: Keep 가로지른 as through and 덩어리 as hunk; SOL’s ‘behemoth’ and ‘other’ are unsupported.
decisions.replacement: The massive hunk of steel that had ground its way through half the battlefield was charging straight toward him and the Hunters.

decisions.reason: ‘the struggle for survival’ is the natural English for 살기 위한 몸부림.
샤오 쉔은 is the subject of 잊은 채; SOL reassigns the forgetting and adds panic-to-escape.
푸푹 is a piercing stab SFX, not a blunt thud.
향해 허물어진다 is collapses toward him; ‘on top of’ jumps the next sentence’s weight beat.
Punchier ‘surged’ and ‘a single step’ for 한 걸음도.
Naturalizes 존재다 and times 숨이 끊기는 마지막 순간 as ‘when,’ not ‘before.’
이걸로 됐어 is ‘this is enough’; SOL adds unsupported ‘Good.’
거체 is the fuselage, not the whole airplane.
SOL drops 처음보다 (‘since the beginning’).
촤아악 is a liquid splash, not a hiss.
뒤집어쓴 is being drenched/dumped on, stronger than ‘covered.’
‘Shouldn’t it normally be’ is the more natural rhetorical for 보통은 … 아닌가.
눈꺼풀을 들어 올렸다 is lifting the eyelids to peek, not merely opening his eyes.
두런두런 is casual murmuring chat, which BASE flattens to ‘chatting.’
Italicize and renumber bangzi at first use, but 도 is ‘too/also,’ not ‘still.’
decisions.replacement: “Then carry them out, Team Leader Choi. Oh, right. Is that bastard who called us *bangzi*[^1] earlier alive, too?”

decisions.reason: Ellipsis matches the 그, hesitation and house style.
Korean splits 어떻게. 왜. and 정리 is organize, not explain.
decisions.replacement: Who, when, where, what, how. Why. Even the five Ws and one H could not organize a scene this bizarre.

decisions.reason: 아니었단 말인가 reverses the CMC assumption; SOL’s ‘Aren’t they’ points the wrong way.
decisions.replacement: *How did the airplane stop so suddenly, and who are those people? So they weren’t Hunters sent by the Central Military Commission?*

decisions.reason: SOL drops 말; he cannot understand the words, not the man.
Fragment ‘Their longtime neighbor’ sets up the 바로 한국이다 reveal.
Next beat identifies one man; 한국인이라면 can stay singular.
‘who stood a full head taller’ is smoother English for 남들보다 머리 하나는 큰.
‘only ever seen’ captures TV에서나 more naturally.
Attaches the Sibeol-jwa footnote at first use after bangzi is [^1].
Cleaner body-tremble line; BASE’s ‘wave’ is extra.
Moves the bangzi footnote to first use.
Renumbers the Sibeol footnote after bangzi-first order.
Removes the duplicate later bangzi footnote.
‘Chinese guy’ matches Taekyung’s casual narration for 중국인.
다가와 / 알은척 is coming up and acting familiar, not ‘pretend they knew me.’
Keeps the imagined English reply as its own thought beat.
The 도대체 complaint is narration, not part of the imagined reply.
승무원 is flight attendants, not generic crew; Inventory capitalization is an unsupported swap.
‘It’s’ is natural spoken English for Choi without losing 입니다 politeness.
정겨운 is fond/heartwarming, closer to ‘comforting’ than ‘pleasant.’
SOL adds ‘gruesome’ and weakens 그 자체라고 할 수 있는 to ‘practically.’
SOL drops 실전 (‘actual/live combat’).
‘clicked my tongue to myself’ naturalizes 내심 혀를 차며.
More spoken rendering of 안 그래도 그럴 생각입니다.
Tighter ‘not the sort to show off’ without losing 결코 과시하려 하지 않을.
빠릿빠릿하게 is a brisk answer, not snapping to attention.
Preserves 그것도 (‘at that’) and 휘장도 (‘also’); SOL is only leaner.
간수해요 is look after/keep, not discipline (‘in line’) or merely grouping (‘together’).
decisions.replacement: “You look like you hold a decent rank, so take care of your men. Let’s save as many people as we can.”

decisions.reason: 대답과 동시에 is answering, not generic speaking.
휩쓴 as ‘swept past’ and 만이 남았다 as ‘only … remained.’
몬스터 놈들을 is ‘those monsters,’ not generic ‘the monsters.’
박혀 is embedded, not buried; 시작된다 does not say ‘anew.’
decisions.replacement: A battle of killing and being killed began. I pulled White Flame from where it was embedded deep in the ground and swung it.

decisions.reason: Naturalizes 물 반, 고기 반 as the crowded-waters idiom; BASE’s ‘half meat’ is a calque.
스쳤다 is grazed, not swept through.
‘them’ avoids repeating ‘notifications’ already stated.
설마 as ‘Don’t tell me’ matches Taekyung’s voice.
‘wondering why’ is more natural for 의아하던.
거의 절반 이상 is ‘roughly half or more,’ not a clean ‘more than half.’
아름답고…용맹하게 are adverbs mocking the manner of disappearing.
Two sentences cleanly split the forgotten-situation beat from 황급히 덧붙였다.
Comma before ‘too’ is indistinguishable.
Preserves 다만, 확신, and the trailing ellipsis into the Lich question.
직접 나선 is stepping in/taking the field, not merely being present.
느껴지는 is sensing life force, not merely that the ogre ‘had’ it.
Technique-first active voice is stronger; 칠공 as all seven orifices is the set phrase.
지나치며 is simultaneous ‘as I passed,’ not sequential ‘passed and.’
Drop BASE’s extra ‘seemed/itself’; keep 몸뚱어리 and 그 사이에, which SOL omits.
decisions.replacement: Space split apart, and the bodies of the monsters caught between the two halves were sliced to pieces.

decisions.reason: ‘who stared’ reduces the dangling modifier without changing the action.
와 함께 is ‘along with,’ not ‘filled the air’; 놈들 are the surviving monsters.
Preserves 파괴력 as destructive power rather than generic ‘powerful.’
‘stammered’ is more natural than ‘spoke in a stammering voice.’
Contraction-only variant; no improvement.
Comma before ‘either’ is indistinguishable.
Clipped ‘Guarantee? What?’ matches 장담? 뭘?
놈의 언데드 통제 is that bastard’s control-ability, not ‘whoever is controlling.’
고민하던 is the kill-or-spare dilemma, not calm ‘considered.’
‘That thing’ is more colloquial for 어쩌구 했던 거.
놈들에 is plural ‘them,’ not SOL’s specified ‘whoever is controlling them.’
Cleaner sequence for 마른침을 꿀꺽 삼킨 나는 as the narrator swallowing.
